sources.observation: Rust 1.97.1 is the patched development release and fixes an LLVM optimization miscompilation.
rustc commit 8bab26f4f68e0e26f0bb7960be334d5b520ea452 embeds Cargo commit c980f4866141969fab6254a680546a277789d6f0.
Rust 1.85.1 is a patch release in the first Edition-2024-capable line.
Rust 1.85.0, not 1.85.1, stabilized Edition 2024.
rustc commit 4eb161250e340c8f48f66e2b929ef4a5bed7c181 embeds Cargo commit d73d2caf9e41a39daf2a8d6ce60ec80bf354d2a7.
rust-version declares a minimum supported compiler and is checked for package targets; it is not a security-support or compatibility proof.
Resolver 3 uses incompatible-rust-version fallback and can still select an incompatible dependency when no compatible candidate exists.
Edition 2024 implies resolver 3, but a virtual workspace must set resolver = 3 explicitly.
Each member must opt into workspace lint inheritance with lints.workspace = true.
Current Cargo can acquire a locked graph before locked, offline floor checks.
rustup 1.29.0 commit 28d1352dbcb436d3111c3594b9e1588e94950464 supports exact patch-version toolchains; minimal profiles require explicit rustfmt and Clippy components.
x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu is an upstream Tier-1 host-tools target; upstream tier status does not prove StatQED workspace support.
Cargo/tar archive handling before the patched release line requires the compatibility floor to remain offline and non-acquiring.
Rust 1.94.1 updated tar to 0.4.45 for CVE-2026-33055 and CVE-2026-33056; Cargo 1.85.1 predates those fixes.
Cargo 1.85.1 is in the affected sparse third-party-registry credential-normalization range.
Cargo versions before Rust 1.96.0 mishandled symlinks from malicious third-party registry tarballs; crates.io was unaffected.
Later Cargo distributions include libssh2 security fixes not present in Cargo 1.85.1.
cargo-audit 0.22.2 remains the current official release; source commit 281452c35cf0870969042374110f099a411bc185.
The production point-in-time scan uses immutable advisory database commit 1237bbe09d2701e14e6593a630fbaf28928df712.
Workflow actions are pinned to full commits and require monitored updates.
Hosted runner labels resolve to mutable images, so each run records observed image metadata without turning it into a cross-platform support claim.
